title: A 45-letter word refuting the toroidal-grid representation-number conjecture of Alshammari, Kitaev and Pyatkin (arXiv:2507.16469, Conjecture 1)
exact_endpoint: Toroidal.mathdb_369421 : ¬ Toroidal.Conjecture1, where Conjecture1 := ∀ m n : ℕ, 3 ≤ m → 3 ≤ n → 8 ≤ m + n → 4 ≤ representationNumber m n; representationNumber = least positive k such that some list over Fin m × Fin n uses every vertex exactly k times and, for distinct vertices, alternation of the two-letter subword holds iff they are adjacent in C_m □ C_n (⊤ if none)
scope: Alshammari-Kitaev-Pyatkin Conjecture 1: R(C_m □ C_n) ≥ 4 for m, n ≥ 3 and m + n ≥ 8. False at (3, 5): an explicit 45-letter 3-uniform word represents C_3 □ C_5, so its representation number is at most 3.

substantive_reason: It refutes an explicit universal conjecture of experts in word-representable graphs, posed after they could not find 3-representations of larger toroidal grids, with a short, fully checkable certificate at the first new case. Significance is modest: a single small certificate, no infinite family or exact values for further tori, found by a solver whose methodology is established.
